The core insight lies in combining inertial measurement units (IMUs) with pseudolite-based GPS augmentation to achieve precise indoor localization. The INS module captures accelerations and gyroscopic rotations, while pseudolites simulate satellite signals indoors. This fusion allows centimeter-level accuracy by mitigating GPS limitations in enclosed environments. The system employs asynchronous pseudolite operation to reduce synchronization overhead and improve robustness. Communication between the ball and orbit processor relies on Zigbee, ensuring low-power, high-reliability data transfer. Power management strategies involve switching off non-critical components when the ball is visible to cameras, leveraging MEMS altitude sensors for triggering events. These primitives form a dual-layered architecture: one for sensing and localization, another for communication and control.
